questions.q: Which three forces do the Heaths say drive behavior change?
a: The rider, the elephant and the path
The goal, the habit and the reward
The mind, the body and the environment
The leader, the team and the culture
questions.why: The overview borrows Jonathan Haidt's rider and elephant image and adds the path they travel.

questions.q: What happens when the rider hears a vague goal like 'eat healthier'?
a: It analyzes endless options and becomes paralyzed
It commits quickly to the first plan it finds
It hands control over to the elephant
It loses interest and gives up entirely
questions.why: Lesson 1 says what looks like resistance is often just a lack of clarity about the next step.

questions.q: Which simple instruction doubled 1% milk sales in West Virginia?
a: Buy 1% milk instead of whole milk
Drink milk only with breakfast
Switch to skim milk entirely
Buy milk in smaller containers
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses this campaign as an example of giving the rider one clear, critical instruction.

questions.q: How did Jon Stegner convince his board that purchasing was wasteful?
a: He piled 424 different pairs of gloves onto the table
He presented a detailed cost report
He showed slides of the factory floor
He invited suppliers to explain their prices
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the mountain of gloves made the problem obvious within seconds and moved the board.

questions.q: What did the campus donation study show about specific requests?
a: Specific requests raised donations even among the 'jerks'
Vague requests worked better for generous people
Character mattered more than how the request was made
Most students refused to donate under any conditions
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a clear request with a map lifted giving to 25% among people rated least generous.
